newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia to export PGMs to Japan from Jun 20 - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russia to export PGMs to Japan from Jun 20 - traders.

text.p: Russia's platinum group metal (PGM) export agency Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) told Japanese clients that exports under 1997 term contracts are expected to begin around June 20, precious metal traders said on Wednesday.
Almaz also said it expected to obtain an export licence by the end of this week, traders said.

"They told us the first delivery from Russia would be around June 20, based on average NYMEX prices between June 15 and June 30, if Almaz obtains the PGM export licence as they said they would," said a trader who met with Almaz representatives for term contract talks.
"The negotiations progressed more smoothly than we had expected, with little disagreement on both prices and the volume we hope to import from Russia (this year)," he said.
According to Almaz, deliveries for July would arrive after July 10 and prices would based on average NYMEX prices during the second-half of June, traders said.
Almaz has long-term supply contracts with 13 or 14 Japanese firms, including major trade houses and bullion houses.
By Wednesday, nearly half of the clients had finished their first round of talks, traders said. Some traders said they would start signing term contract documents on Thursday.

Japanese imports of Russian palladium under 1997 term contracts are likely to decline from last year as end-users, particularly in the electronics industry, are increasingly reluctant to use the metal due to its high and volatile prices, traders said.

Demand from Japanese electronic firms, who use palladium to make capacitors, is expected to weaken as they step up efforts to use cheaper substitutes such as nickel and also miniaturise their products, traders said.
"With a few exceptions, most Japanese clients were hoping to cut palladium imports from Russia slightly this year," the trader said.

Japan's palladium imports from Russia under term contracts for 1996 were estimated at around 38 tonnes. Total imports last year were about 77.4 tonnes, of which about 50 tonnes were of Russian origin.
One trading house source, who declined to be named, said his company hoped to reduce Russian palladium imports by nearly 30 percent this year, after buying about six tonnes last year.

"Last year, we held internal meetings almost every day on how to sell the surplus palladium we had. The sharp rise in palladium prices recently is likely to weigh on palladium demand from the electronic sector," the trader said.
There were a few trading houses which said they wanted to increase their monthly import volume from last year partly in an attempt to cool the abnormally overheated lease market.
Expectations that demand from the auto catalyst sector would grow also prompted some trading houses to ask for more palladium, traders said.
Palladium short-term lease rates skyrocketed to nearly 100 percent on Wednesday, while platinum lease rates stood at 50 percent. Normally lease rates for both metals are around two to three percent.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals (PGM), and Russia supplies more than 60 percent of global demand for palladium.
